review_comments.body:
### Passkeys broken on initial login due to user-null check **High Severity** The `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` method requires `user != null`, but the `authenticate` method calls it when `context.getUser()` is null during initial login. Previously, `fillContextForm` was called inside the `else` block (when user was null), setting up the passkeys conditional UI on the first login page. Now it's gated behind `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` which returns `false` when user is null, so passkeys won't render on the initial login form. The `user != null` condition in this method should likely be removed.
Additional Locations (1) - [`services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java#L114-L116`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-keycloak/blob/3214b188de808fdb0fff335556b686f1b0a63218/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java#L114-L116)

### Challenge method passkeys condition completely inverted from original **Medium Severity** The `challenge` error method's condition was inverted from `context.getUser() == null` to effectively `context.getUser() != null` (via `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled`). While this fixes the re-authentication error case (user is set), it also means passkeys are no longer shown after an invalid-username error where user remains null. The original code intentionally set up passkeys when the user was not yet identified during error recovery.

### Test cleanup uses wrong hardcoded alias string **Medium Severity** The test cleanup registers removal of an IDP with the hardcoded literal `"alias"` instead of the actual alias (e.g., `"idp-alias-" + i` at line 381 and `"idp-alias-20"` at line 425). Since no IDP with alias `"alias"` is ever created, the cleanup will fail to remove the 20+ identity providers created during the test, causing test resource leakage that could affect other tests.
Additional Locations (1) - [`testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java#L424-L425`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-keycloak/blob/3e597722a9164d145bc46aa1de5bd714fb6ba357/testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java#L424-L425)

prs.title: Add AuthzClientCryptoProvider for authorization client cryptographic operations

review_comments.body: ### Dead code: unused ASN1Encoder writes are discarded **Low Severity** Two `ASN1Encoder.create().write(...)` calls on lines 114–115 create encoder instances, write `rBigInteger` and `sBigInteger` to them, then immediately discard the results. The actual DER encoding is performed by the separate encoder chain starting on line 117. These statements appear to be leftover from development and serve no purpose. Comparing with the equivalent `BCECDSACryptoProvider.concatenatedRSToASN1DER`, no such redundant writes exist.

prs.title: Add rolling-updates feature flag and compatibility framework
Add Client resource type and scopes to authorization schema

review_comments.body: ### Event listener guard misses V2 feature flag **High Severity** The event handler guard checks only `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (V1), but `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is an independent feature (depends on `AUTHORIZATION`, not V1). When only V2 is enabled, `RoleRemovedEvent` and `GroupRemovedEvent` handlers won't fire, leaving stale permission data. The V2 `MgmtPermissionsV2` inherits `roles()` and `groups()` from V1 and those cleanup paths work correctly — they're just never reached. Every other method in `AdminPermissions` checks `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`; this is the only one that doesn't.

### Unused private method `getEvaluationContext` is dead code **Low Severity** The private method `getEvaluationContext` in `ClientPermissionsV2` is never called. The only method that would logically use it, `canExchangeTo`, throws `UnsupportedOperationException` instead. This appears to be leftover code copied from the parent class `ClientPermissions.canExchangeTo`.

prs.title: Add Groups resource type and scopes to authorization schema

review_comments.body: ### `canManage()` grants access with VIEW-only permission **High Severity** `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` checks for both `AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW` and `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` scopes, meaning a user with only `VIEW` permission on groups can pass management authorization checks. This is inconsistent with `canManage(GroupModel)` which correctly only checks `MANAGE`. The analogous `ClientPermissionsV2.canManage()` also correctly only checks `MANAGE`. Since `canManage()` guards write operations like `addTopLevelGroup()` via `requireManage()`, this allows view-only users to create/modify groups.

### `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` uses resource ID not group ID **High Severity** `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` uses `groupResource.getId()` (internal resource UUID) instead of `groupResource.getName()` (group model ID) in two places. The `hasPermission` method expects a group model ID (it does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`), so passing the internal resource ID causes the lookup to fail, falling through to only the global permission check. The returned set also contains resource UUIDs instead of group model IDs, breaking downstream user filtering via `UserModel.GROUPS`. The analogous `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission` correctly uses `resource.getName()`.

This will display incorrect character variants to `zh_CN` users. The Traditional Chinese `zh_TW` file already has its own correct translation.

### Substring indices can overlap causing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException **Low Severity** The `start` and `end` counters that strip identical prefix/suffix characters are computed independently and can overlap when the shorter string's prefix and suffix together span its full length. This mismatch will cause the placeholders and `{2,choice,...}` expression to render as literal text instead of being substituted with actual values.

prs.title: Implement access token context encoding framework

review_comments.body: ### Null check validates wrong variable (copy-paste error) **High Severity** The `Objects.requireNonNull` on line 73 checks `grantType` a second time instead of `rawTokenId`. The error message says "Null rawTokenId not allowed" but the actual variable being checked is `grantType`. This means a null `rawTokenId` will silently pass validation and be stored, which could cause `NullPointerException`s later when encoding or using the token ID.

### Test matcher uses wrong substring indices for grant **High Severity** The `isAccessTokenId` matcher extracts the grant type shortcut using `substring(3, 5)`, but the encoded token format is `sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantType(2) + ':' + rawTokenId`, so the grant shortcut is at indices 4–5. The correct call is `substring(4, 6)`.

### Test matcher inverts grant type equality check logic **High Severity** The `isAccessTokenId` matcher returns `false` when the grant shortcut *matches* the expected value, which is the opposite of the intended behavior. The condition `if (items[0].substring(...).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false` rejects valid tokens and accepts invalid ones. The `equals` check needs to be negated.

### Client credentials grant never sets grant type attribute **Medium Severity** `ClientCredentialsGrantType` calls `tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken()` directly without ever setting `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` on the `clientSessionCtx`. Every other grant type sets this attribute (via `createTokenResponse` in the base class, or explicitly), but `ClientCredentialsGrantType` has its own token-creation flow and was missed. The resulting token IDs will encode the grant type as `"na"` (unknown) instead of `"cc"`.

prs.title: Implement recovery key support for user storage providers

review_comments.body: ### Missing null check causes potential NPE in getCredentials **Low Severity** `getCredentials` calls `getMyUser(user)` but doesn't null-check the result before accessing `myUser.recoveryCodes` and `myUser.otp`. Other methods in the same class like `isValid`, `isConfiguredFor`, and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` all perform null checks on the value returned by `getMyUser`. This inconsistency could lead to a `NullPointerException` if the user isn't found in the map.

### Credential ID lost when creating model from values **Medium Severity** In `getCredentials`, the recovery code credential is rebuilt via `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)`, which does not set the credential's ID. The original ID stored in `myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()` (assigned during `updateCredential`) is never carried over to the new model. This contrasts with OTP credentials in the same method, which are returned directly with their ID intact. The resulting credential has a null ID, making it unfindable by ID in the federated credentials stream.

prs.title: Fix concurrent group access to prevent NullPointerException

review_comments.body: ### Returning null violates interface's non-null contract **High Severity** The `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` interface contract explicitly states it "Never returns `null`," but this new implementation returns `null` when `modelSupplier.get()` is `null`. This trades one `NullPointerException` (calling a method on a null model) for another at the call site — for example, `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` passes the result directly to `setSubGroupCount`, and any caller that auto-unboxes the `Long` to `long` will still crash. Returning `0L` instead of `null` would satisfy the contract.
